decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 4.75% to 5%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: Job gains have picked up in recent months and are running at a robust pace; the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.”
Reworded from the previous statement: “Inflation has eased somewhat but remains elevated.”

changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.

The Committee anticipates that some additional policy firming may be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 19.07% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.48% and moved -11 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.73% would fall by about $21.87 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 275k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 6% over the past year (February 2023); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 4.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -21 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -1.65%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.23% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 21%, cut 1%, hike 78%.
